title: Enchiladas
subtitle: Corn tortillas filled with chicken and baked in a chilli sauce
excerpt: The classic Mexican baked tortilla dish: corn tortillas briefly fried, filled with shredded chicken and cheese, rolled and laid in a dish, covered in a red chilli sauce and more cheese, and baked until molten and bubbling.

recipe.sourceNotes: Enchiladas are one of the great Mexican antojitos (street snacks elevated to a proper meal), with a history stretching back to pre-Columbian Aztec cooking in which corn tortillas were dipped in chilli sauce and eaten as a staple food. The English word enchilada comes from enchilar (to season with chilli). In Mexico, enchiladas are regional and specific: Enchiladas verdes use green tomatillo sauce, enchiladas mole use dark mole sauce, enmoladas are a variant, enchiladas suizas are made with cream. The red chilli sauce version (enchiladas rojas) is perhaps the most internationally recognisable. Corn tortillas are essential; wheat flour tortillas, while acceptable, give a softer, less authentic result. The brief frying of the tortillas before filling softens them so they roll without cracking and prevents them absorbing too much sauce and becoming mushy during baking.

recipeTools.notes: A baking dish large enough to hold 12 enchiladas in a single layer.

content.text: Fry each corn tortilla in oil for about 10 seconds per side, long enough to soften but not to crisp. They should be pliable enough to roll without cracking. Dip briefly in the warm sauce before filling so the tortilla absorbs flavour and is easier to roll. The enchiladas can be assembled several hours ahead and refrigerated; add 5 minutes to the baking time if cooking from cold.

items.preparation: grated; or a mix of cheddar and mozzarella
ancho or guajillo chillies, soaked in boiling water for 20 minutes then drained
2 tbsp for the sauce, 2 tbsp for frying the tortillas

content.text: Make the sauce: soften the onion in 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika and cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and soaked chillies. Simmer for 15 minutes, then blend until smooth. Season with salt. The sauce should be pourable but not thin.

Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan). Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Briefly fry each tortilla for 10 seconds per side until pliable. Dip in the warm sauce, place a spoonful of shredded chicken and a little cheese in the centre, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in a baking dish. Repeat with all tortillas.

Pour the remaining sauce over the rolled enchiladas, covering them completely. Scatter the remaining cheese over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the cheese is melted and the sauce is bubbling. Serve immediately with soured cream and fresh coriander.
